podcast.body: This early 1960s vocal ensemble hit is referenced as a comparison point for TLC's "Ain't 2 Proud 2 Beg," which was described as its "blunter 90s equivalent." "You can think of it as the blunter 90s equivalent of the sherels will you love me tomorrow."

podcast.body: Written by Gerry Goffin and Carole King, this song was chosen by Don Kirshner as the follow-up to "Tonight the Night." It featured lyrics by Goffin that brought a new depth to pop music, discussing female adolescent emotion and a woman's worry about being a one-night stand. Carole King wrote the string arrangement overnight, drawing inspiration from The Drifters' "There Goes My Baby," despite never having written for an orchestra before. The group initially disliked the song, finding it sounded like a country song, but Luther Dixon insisted on its release, leading to it becoming a number one hit. "The group didn't like the song, thinking it sounded like a country song, but Luther Dixon insisted, and the result went to number one."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
